mainTopic: Two pairs of תפילין on שבת and the search for the תנא who holds that שבת is a time for תפילין
overview: The משנה discusses someone who finds תפילין outside on שבת and brings them in by wearing them. The תנא קמא (רבי מאיר) allows one pair at a time, while רבן גמליאל allows two. The גמרא first offers another explanation: all agree that fulfilling a מצוה needs no כוונה, and they argue whether violating בל תוסיף needs כוונה. It then proposes that they argue about violating בל תוסיף at the wrong time (שלא בזמנו), but it rejects this with two challenges, and it returns to the earlier answers. Next the גמרא asks which תנא holds that שבת is a time for תפילין. It suggests רבי עקיבא, who reads the verse ״ושמרת את החקה הזאת״ as only about פסח, and it defends that reading against a challenge from רבי אבין's rule about ״השמר״. But a ברייתא shows that רבי עקיבא excludes שבת because it is itself an אות. The גמרא then tries רבי נתן, who allows תפילין at night, but it rejects that proof as well. Finally it suggests the חכמים who did not stop מיכל בת כושי from wearing תפילין, and it begins to push back on that proof, a discussion that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: New explanation: the argument is about כוונה for violating בל תוסיף
steps.stepSummary: Everyone agrees that fulfilling a מצוה does not require כוונה. The argument is only about whether violating בל תוסיף requires כוונה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or, if you prefer, say this: everyone agrees that to fulfill a מצוה you don't need intent. Here they argue about what it takes to violate 'Do not add.' The תנא קמא holds that violating בל תוסיף does not need intent. רבן גמליאל holds that violating בל תוסיף does need intent.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers another way to explain why the תנא קמא allows only one pair of תפילין while רבן גמליאל allows two.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here both sides agree that fulfilling a מצוה works even without כוונה. The only open question is whether the 'adding' sin of בל תוסיף also happens automatically. The תנא קמא says it does, so a second pair is forbidden. רבן גמליאל says you only violate it if you intend to do a מצוה, and someone rescuing תפילין has no such intent, so a second pair is fine.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you wish, say (introduces an alternative explanation)
To fulfill (one's obligation of a מצוה)
To violate (a prohibition)
The prohibition 'Do not add' to the Torah's מצוות
Intent
They disagree

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up 'to fulfill' (לצאת) and 'to violate' (לעבור). In this explanation, both sides agree about לצאת. The argument is only about לעבור.

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:

phrases.aramaic: דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא לָצֵאת לָא בָּעֵי כַּוּוֹנָה,
phrases.english: Everyone agrees that to fulfill a מצוה one does not need intent,
and here they disagree about violating 'Do not add,'
for the first tanna holds:

phrases.aramaic: לַעֲבוֹר מִשּׁוּם ״בַּל תּוֹסִיף״ לָא בָּעֵי כַּוּוֹנָה.
phrases.english: to violate 'Do not add,' one does not need intent.
And Rabban Gamliel holds:
to violate 'Do not add,' one needs intent.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא: דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא לָצֵאת לָא בָּעֵי כַּוּוֹנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers an alternative to the earlier explanation(s) of the משנה's disagreement, on the previous amud.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Relocating the disagreement to a different legal question
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The argument might have been about whether fulfilling a מצוה requires כוונה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both sides agree about fulfilling. They argue only about whether violating בל תוסיף requires כוונה.

steps.title: Another explanation begins: if שבת were a time for תפילין, כוונה would not matter
steps.stepSummary: Setup for a third explanation. If שבת were a time for תפילין, everyone would agree that כוונה is needed neither for violating nor for fulfilling.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or, if you prefer, say this: if we held that שבת is a time for תפילין, everyone would agree that you need no intent to violate, and no intent to fulfill.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a new explanation. It first describes the situation where there would be no argument at all, to prepare for the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This line assumes that if שבת were a proper time for תפילין, both sides would agree that intent changes nothing. That would leave no room for their argument. The hidden implication is that the real dispute must assume שבת is NOT a time for תפילין, which the next step spells out.

keyTerms.meaning: If we were to hold
A proper time for wearing תפילין

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:

phrases.aramaic: אִי דִּסְבִירָא לַן דְּשַׁבָּת זְמַן תְּפִילִּין —
phrases.english: if we were to hold that Shabbat is a time for phylacteries —

phrases.aramaic: דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא לָא לַעֲבוֹר בָּעֵי כַּוּוֹנָה
phrases.english: everyone would agree that one needs no intent to violate
and no intent to fulfill.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא: אִי דִּסְבִירָא לַן דְּשַׁבָּת זְמַן תְּפִילִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a further alternative explanation by first ruling out a scenario where no argument could exist.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Setup: narrowing down the framework for the dispute
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One might think the argument could exist even if שבת is a time for תפילין.
steps.terutzMaskana: If שבת were a time for תפילין, there would be nothing to argue about. So the dispute must assume שבת is not a time for תפילין.

steps.title: The argument is about violating at the wrong time (שלא בזמנו)
steps.stepSummary: Since שבת is not a time for תפילין, they argue about whether violating בל תוסיף at the wrong time requires כוונה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But here they argue about violating 'out of its time.' The תנא קמא holds that no intent is needed. רבן גמליאל holds that violating out of its time does need intent.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא completes the new explanation. The dispute is about doing a מצוה at a time when it is not commanded.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On שבת, wearing תפילין is 'out of its time.' The תנא קמא says that doing the act at the wrong time violates בל תוסיף even without intent, so only one pair is allowed. רבן גמליאל says you only violate at the wrong time if you intend to do the מצוה, so rescuing with two pairs is fine.

keyTerms.meaning: Not in its proper time
The first (anonymous) opinion in the משנה

steps.whatToRemember: There are now several possible explanations of the משנה's argument. The latest: on שבת (not a time for תפילין), the תנא קמא says violating בל תוסיף שלא בזמנו needs no כוונה, while רבן גמליאל says it does.

phrases.english: But here they disagree about 'violating not in its time.'

phrases.aramaic: תַּנָּא קַמָּא סָבַר: לָא בָּעֵי כַּוּוֹנָה.
phrases.english: The first tanna holds: one does not need intent.
And Rabban Gamliel holds:
to violate not in its time, one needs intent.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the explanation that step 2 set up.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Relocating the disagreement to violation שלא בזמנו
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The argument might be about כוונה in general.
steps.terutzMaskana: The argument is specifically about whether violating בל תוסיף out of a מצוה's time requires כוונה.

steps.title: Challenge: by this logic, רבי מאיר should forbid even one pair
steps.stepSummary: If the תנא קמא (רבי מאיר) holds that wearing תפילין out of time violates בל תוסיף even without כוונה, then even one pair should be forbidden on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, according to רבי מאיר, even one pair should not be allowed!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the explanation from step 3.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר is the תנא קמא who allows one pair. On שבת, which is not a time for תפילין, even the first pair is 'added' at the wrong time. If no כוונה is needed to violate, then wearing even one pair should violate בל תוסיף, yet the משנה lets him wear one pair.

keyTerms.meaning: If so (introduces a challenge built on what was just said)
One pair (of תפילין)
Also not / not even

steps.confusionAlert: רבי מאיר here is the same person as the תנא קמא in the משנה. The challenge works because his own ruling (one pair is allowed) clashes with the reasoning just given for him.

phrases.english: If so,

phrases.aramaic: לְרַבִּי מֵאִיר זוּג אֶחָד נָמֵי לָא.
phrases.english: according to Rabbi Meir, not even one pair should be allowed.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, לְרַבִּי מֵאִיר זוּג אֶחָד נָמֵי לָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the explanation given in steps 2–3.
steps.kashyaTarget: The explanation that the תנא קמא holds violating בל תוסיף שלא בזמנו requires no כוונה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If wearing תפילין out of time violates בל תוסיף without intent, then even the first pair on שבת violates it. That contradicts רבי מאיר's ruling that one pair is allowed.

steps.title: Sleeping in the סוכה on the Eighth Day
steps.stepSummary: A second challenge to the third explanation: if adding to a מצוה out of its time violates בל תוסיף even without כוונה, then sleeping in a סוכה on שמיני should earn lashes.
steps.simpleTranslation: And furthermore: one who sleeps in a סוכה on the eighth day should be flogged!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a second attack on the third explanation. If doing a מצוה out of its time breaks בל תוסיף even without intending to, then a person who sleeps in a סוכה on שמיני עצרת would deserve lashes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The third explanation said that a מצוה done at the wrong time counts as adding to the Torah even without כוונה. But outside ארץ ישראל, Jews sit in the סוכה on the eighth day because of the doubt about the calendar. Nobody thinks they deserve lashes, so the premise must be wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: And furthermore; introduces an additional challenge
The eighth day, שמיני עצרת, which comes after the seven days of סוכות
He should receive lashes, the punishment for violating a Torah prohibition

phrases.english: And furthermore: one who sleeps on the eighth day
in a sukkah should be flogged!
phrases.notes: He would be adding an eighth day to a seven-day מצוה, which would be בל תוסיף.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second, independent challenge to the third explanation, alongside the challenge in step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: The third explanation's claim that doing a מצוה out of its time violates בל תוסיף even without כוונה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Under that claim, sleeping in a סוכה on שמיני would be a punishable violation. Standard practice shows it is not.

steps.title: Return to the Original Answers
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא drops the third explanation and says the earlier explanations stand.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is clear as we answered originally.
steps.whatsHappening: Since the third explanation has fallen apart, the גמרא says to go back to the earlier explanations it gave.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two challenges in steps 4 and 5 knock out the idea that out-of-time performance breaks בל תוסיף without כוונה. The דיון about two pairs of תפילין on שבת is explained by the earlier approaches instead.

keyTerms.meaning: It is clear; signals that a proposed answer is rejected and an earlier one is kept
As we answered originally

steps.whatToRemember: The third explanation, that out-of-time performance violates בל תוסיף without כוונה, is rejected. The earlier explanations remain.

phrases.english: Rather, it is clear
as we answered originally.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the result of steps 4 and 5: the third explanation is abandoned.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The third explanation is rejected, and the earlier explanations hold.

steps.title: Who Holds That שבת Is a Time for תפילין?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which תנא holds that שבת is a proper time for wearing תפילין.
steps.simpleTranslation: And whom have you heard say that שבת is a time for תפילין?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a clarifying question to set up the next step: which known תנא actually holds that one may wear תפילין on שבת?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier in the סוגיא, the possibility that שבת is a time for תפילין came up. Now the גמרא wants to anchor that view in a specific תנא.

keyTerms.meaning: Whom have you heard say; asks for the source of an opinion
A time when the מצוה of תפילין applies

phrases.english: And whom have you heard
who holds Shabbat is a time for tefillin?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַאן שָׁמְעַתְּ לֵיהּ שַׁבָּת זְמַן תְּפִילִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Picks up a premise raised earlier, that שבת might be a time for תפילין, and asks who holds it.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The name of the תנא who holds that שבת is a time for תפילין.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא; רבי יוסי הגלילי's Opposing Reading
steps.stepSummary: The answer is רבי עקיבא. The גמרא brings a ברייתא in which רבי יוסי הגלילי learns from the verse that תפילין are not worn at night or on שבת and יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא. As it was taught: 'And you shall keep this ordinance in its season from days to days.' 'Days' and not nights. 'From days' and not all days, excluding שבתות and ימים טובים. These are the words of רבי יוסי הגלילי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the view is רבי עקיבא's and begins quoting a ברייתא to show it. First comes the opposing opinion of רבי יוסי הגלילי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי הגלילי reads the verse at the end of the תפילין section as applying to תפילין. The word ימים excludes nights. The extra letter מ in מימים means 'some days, not all,' which excludes שבת and יום טוב. This is the view רבי עקיבא will reject.

keyTerms.meaning: As was taught in a ברייתא
Ordinance or statute
From days to days; read here as limiting which days
Excluding

steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא opens with רבי יוסי הגלילי, but the answer to the question is רבי עקיבא. His opinion comes in the next line and disagrees with רבי יוסי הגלילי.

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva. As it was taught:
"And you shall keep this ordinance
in its season from days to days."
phrases.notes: This is the פסוק in שמות יג:י, at the end of the section about תפילין and פסח.

phrases.english: "Days": and not nights.
"From days": and not all days,
phrases.notes: The prefix מ ('from') is read as limiting: some days, not all.

phrases.english: excluding Shabbatot and festivals,
these are the words of Rabbi Yosei HaGelili.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 7 and begins the supporting ברייתא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי עקיבא, as the ברייתא's dispute shows. First comes רבי יוסי הגלילי's opposing derivation.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא Limits the Verse to פסח
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא says the verse refers only to פסח. So there is no source excluding שבת from תפילין.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא says: This ordinance was said only regarding פסח.
steps.whatsHappening: This line is the actual proof. רבי עקיבא says the verse is about the קרבן פסח, not תפילין, so it does not remove שבת from the time of תפילין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the only source excluding שבת is taken away from תפילין, רבי עקיבא would hold that שבת is a time for תפילין. This confirms the answer given in step 8.

keyTerms.meaning: With regard to the קרבן פסח
Only

steps.whyThisMatters: It ties the earlier view that 'שבת is a time for תפילין' to a named תנא. It also sets up the next challenge, which grows out of reading the verse as being about פסח.

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva says:
This ordinance was not said
except regarding Pesach alone.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר: לֹא נֶאֱמַר חוּקָּה זוֹ אֶלָּא לְעִנְיַן פֶּסַח בִּלְבַד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא and proves the answer from step 8.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי עקיבא holds שבת is a time for תפילין.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא in which רבי עקיבא limits ״ושמרת את החקה הזאת״ to פסח.

steps.title: Does the משנה Contradict רבי עקיבא?
steps.stepSummary: A משנה calls פסח and מילה positive commandments only. But if the verse ״ושמרת״ is about פסח, as רבי עקיבא says, פסח should also carry a negative commandment.
steps.simpleTranslation: But that which we learned: פסח and מילה are positive commandments. Shall we say it is not like רבי עקיבא? For if it were רבי עקיבא, since he applies the verse to פסח, there is also a negative commandment, according to רבי אבין in the name of רבי אילעאי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי עקיבא's reading. A משנה lists פסח as only a מצות עשה. Under רבי עקיבא, though, the word ושמרת in the verse would add a לא תעשה to פסח, so the משנה would not match his view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה (in כריתות) treats פסח and מילה as positive commandments only. If the verse ״ושמרת״ refers to פסח, then by רבי אבין's rule it creates a negative commandment as well. That would make the משנה disagree with רבי עקיבא, which the גמרא is reluctant to accept.

keyTerms.meaning: That we learned in a משנה
A positive commandment
Shall we say; proposes a troubling conclusion
A negative commandment
He applies it to; he interprets the verse as referring to

phrases.english: But that which we learned:
Pesach and circumcision are positive commandments,
shall we say it is not like Rabbi Akiva?
For if it were Rabbi Akiva,
since he applies the verse to Pesach,
there is also a negative commandment,
according to Rabbi Avin, who said in the name of Rabbi Elai.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֶלָּא הָא דִּתְנַן: הַפֶּסַח וְהַמִּילָה מִצְוַת עֲשֵׂה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the consequence of רבי עקיבא's reading from step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי עקיבא's position that ״ושמרת את החקה הזאת״ refers to פסח.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Under רבי אבין's rule, ושמרת marks a לא תעשה. Then פסח would carry a negative commandment, which contradicts the משנה that lists it only as a מצות עשה.

steps.title: רבי אבין's Rule: 'Guard,' 'Lest,' 'Do Not'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי אבין in the name of רבי אילעאי: wherever the Torah says השמר, פן, or אל, it is a negative commandment.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבי אבין said in the name of רבי אילעאי: Wherever it says 'guard,' 'lest,' or 'do not,' it is nothing other than a negative commandment!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the rule behind its challenge. Words like 'guard yourself,' 'lest,' and 'do not' always mark a negative commandment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under this rule, ושמרת (from the root שמר) turns the verse into a לא תעשה. If the verse is about פסח, as רבי עקיבא says, פסח carries a לאו, which sharpens the contradiction with the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: Guard yourself; a Torah wording that signals a prohibition
Lest
A negative commandment

steps.confusionAlert: ושמרת sounds like a positive instruction ('keep it'), but by this rule any wording from the root שמר signals a prohibition.

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי אָבִין אָמַר רַבִּי אִילְעַאי:
phrases.english: As Rabbi Avin said in the name of Rabbi Elai:
Any place where it is said
"guard," "lest," or "do not,"
it is nothing other than a negative commandment!

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי אָבִין אָמַר רַבִּי אִילְעַאי: כׇּל מָקוֹם שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר הִשָּׁמֶר פֶּן וְאַל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the rule that the challenge in step 10 relies on.
steps.raayaObject: That the verse ״ושמרת״, if applied to פסח, creates a negative commandment.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי אבין's rule in the name of רבי אילעאי about השמר, פן, and אל.

steps.title: השמר on a positive מצוה counts as a positive מצוה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא defends רבי עקיבא. ״השמר״ creates a לאו only when it is attached to a negative command. When it is attached to a positive command, it is a positive command (עשה). So פסח can be about ״ושמרת״ and still have only positive commandments.
steps.simpleTranslation: You can even say this follows רבי עקיבא. ״השמר״ said about a negative command is a negative command. ״השמר״ said about a positive command is a positive command.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 10. It explains why ״ושמרת״ about פסח does not turn פסח into a negative commandment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule of רבי אבין (step 11) says ״השמר״ means a לאו. The גמרא now limits that rule: ״השמר״ takes on the character of the מצוה it is guarding. Since פסח is a positive מצוה, the ״ושמרת״ there is only a positive command, so the משנה calling פסח only an עשה is correct even according to רבי עקיבא.

keyTerms.meaning: Even if you say: you can hold this opinion and still avoid the problem
Be careful / guard: a Torah word that can signal a commandment
A negative commandment, a 'do not'
A positive commandment, a 'do'

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think this cancels the rule of רבי אבין. The rule still holds for negative commandments. It only does not create a לאו when ״השמר״ is guarding a positive מצוה.

phrases.english: You can even say it follows Rabbi Akiva,
'Observe' said about a negative command is a negative command,
phrases.notes: When ״השמר״ guards a 'do not', it adds a לאו.

phrases.english: 'Observe' said about a positive command is a positive command.
phrases.notes: פסח is a positive מצוה, so its ״ושמרת״ is only an עשה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 10 by narrowing the rule quoted in step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting a principle: ״השמר״ follows the type of the מצוה it guards
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Every ״השמר״ creates a negative commandment, so פסח would have a לאו according to רבי עקיבא.
steps.terutzMaskana: ״השמר״ on a positive מצוה is only an עשה, so פסח has no לאו and the משנה fits רבי עקיבא.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא himself excludes שבת from תפילין
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: does רבי עקיבא really hold that שבת is a time for תפילין? A ברייתא shows he learns from ״לאות״ that תפילין are not worn on שבת and יום טוב, because those days are themselves a sign.
steps.simpleTranslation: And does רבי עקיבא really hold that שבת is a time for תפילין? But a ברייתא teaches: רבי עקיבא says, I might think a person should put on תפילין on שבת and יום טוב. So the verse says, 'It shall be a sign for you on your arm': only those who need a sign wear them. These days are excluded, because they themselves are a sign.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer from step 8. It brings a ברייתא where רבי עקיבא clearly says no תפילין on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 9 the גמרא argued that רבי עקיבא has no source to exclude שבת, since he reads ״ושמרת״ as only about פסח. But this ברייתא gives רבי עקיבא a different source: the word ״אות״. Since שבת and יום טוב are already a sign between us and ה׳, no extra sign of תפילין is needed, so רבי עקיבא cannot be the תנא we are looking for.

keyTerms.meaning: But it was taught in a ברייתא: introduces a source that contradicts
I might have thought: introduces a possible mistaken idea
Therefore the verse says: introduces the verse that teaches otherwise
A sign
They themselves are a sign

steps.whyThisMatters: This idea, that שבת and יום טוב are themselves an אות and so תפילין are not worn then, is the well-known reason for the practice of not wearing תפילין on those days.

phrases.english: And does Rabbi Akiva hold
that Shabbat is a time for tefillin?!
phrases.notes: A surprised question that works as a challenge.

phrases.english: But it was taught: Rabbi Akiva says:
I might think a person should put on tefillin
on Shabbatot and Festivals,
Therefore the verse says:
'And it shall be for a sign for you on your arm,'
phrases.notes: This is the פסוק in שמות יג:ט.

phrases.english: those who need a sign,
phrases.notes: Tefillin are for days when a sign is needed.

phrases.english: these are excluded, since they themselves are a sign.
phrases.notes: שבת and יום טוב already serve as a sign.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְסָבַר רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא שַׁבָּת זְמַן תְּפִילִּין הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Having defended רבי עקיבא about פסח, the גמרא now attacks the original claim that he allows תפילין on שבת.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer of step 8, that רבי עקיבא is the תנא who holds שבת is a time for תפילין.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An explicit ברייתא quotes רבי עקיבא excluding שבת and יום טוב from תפילין, using the word ״אות״.

steps.title: A new answer: רבי נתן, who allows תפילין at night
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives a new answer: the תנא is רבי נתן. He holds that one who is awake at night may keep wearing תפילין. Since night is a time for תפילין for him, the גמרא concludes שבת is also a time for תפילין.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is this תנא, as a ברייתא teaches: Someone awake at night may take off his תפילין if he wants, or keep them on if he wants. These are the words of רבי נתן. יונתן הקיטוני says: we do not put on תפילין at night. Since for the first תנא night is a time for תפילין, שבת is also a time for תפילין.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops רבי עקיבא and suggests a different answer to the question of step 7. It points to רבי נתן and reasons from his view on night to a view on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי הגלילי (step 8) learned from one verse that night and שבת are both excluded together. רבי נתן allows night, so he must not accept that verse as excluding anything. The גמרא assumes that without that verse there is no reason to exclude שבת either, so רבי נתן would hold שבת is a time for תפילין.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather: drops the earlier answer and gives a new one
One who is awake at night
Takes off (the תפילין)
Puts on / keeps on (the תפילין)
The first תנא: the first opinion in a ברייתא or משנה

phrases.english: Rather, it is this tanna, as it was taught:
One who is awake at night,
if he wants, he removes them; if he wants, he keeps them on,
these are the words of Rabbi Natan.
Yonatan HaKitoni says:
We do not put on tefillin at night.
Since for the first tanna night is a time for tefillin —
phrases.notes: The גמרא now draws its own inference from the ברייתא.

phrases.english: Shabbat is also a time for tefillin.
phrases.notes: Because night and שבת were excluded together by the same verse.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Since step 13 knocked out רבי עקיבא, the גמרא offers a replacement answer to the question of step 7.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא holds that שבת is a time for תפילין (from step 7).
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי נתן, who allows תפילין at night, and so presumably on שבת too.

steps.title: Night may be allowed while Shabbat is still excluded
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. Maybe רבי נתן allows night but still excludes שבת. We know רבי עקיבא holds exactly that: night is a time for תפילין, but שבת is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: Maybe he holds that night is a time for תפילין, but שבת is not a time for תפילין. For we heard that רבי עקיבא says: night is a time for תפילין, but שבת is not a time for תפילין!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes away the proof from רבי נתן. It shows that allowing night does not force you to allow שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 14 assumed that night and שבת always go together. But רבי עקיבא proves they can be split: he rejects רבי יוסי הגלילי's verse, so he allows night, yet he excludes שבת for a different reason, the ״אות״ verse (step 13). רבי נתן could hold the same way, so we still have not found a clear תנא who allows תפילין on שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: Perhaps: introduces another possibility that weakens a proof
He holds
We have heard him: we know his opinion from another source
Night

steps.whatToRemember: There are two separate reasons to exclude days from תפילין: the verse ״מימים ימימה״ of רבי יוסי הגלילי (night and שבת together), and the ״אות״ reason of רבי עקיבא (only שבת and יום טוב). Allowing night does not prove that one allows שבת.

phrases.english: Perhaps he holds
night is a time for tefillin,
but Shabbat is not a time for tefillin.

phrases.aramaic: דְּהָא שָׁמְעִינַן לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא דְּאָמַר:
phrases.english: For we have heard that Rabbi Akiva said:
night is a time for tefillin,
phrases.notes: He reads ״ושמרת״ as only about פסח, so night is not excluded.

phrases.english: but Shabbat is not a time for tefillin!
phrases.notes: Because of the ״אות״ reason from step 13.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּילְמָא סְבִירָא לֵיהּ לַיְלָה זְמַן תְּפִילִּין הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the inference of step 14 by showing that night and שבת can be separated.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the inference from רבי נתן's view on night to his view on שבת, not his ruling about night.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Step 14 assumed night and שבת must go together. רבי עקיבא shows one can allow night yet exclude שבת because of ״אות״.

steps.title: A new candidate: the Sages who let Michal wear tefillin
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא proposes a new תנא who holds that שבת is a time for תפילין. It is the חכמים who did not protest when מיכל בת כושי wore תפילין. This shows they consider תפילין a מצוה that is not bound by time.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is this תנא, as a ברייתא teaches: מיכל, the daughter of כושי (שאול המלך), used to put on תפילין, and the חכמים did not protest. The wife of יונה used to go up to ירושלים for the festival, and the חכמים did not protest. Since the חכמים did not protest against her, it is clear that they hold that תפילין is a positive מצוה that is not bound by time.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives up on רבי נתן and offers a new source for the view that שבת is a time for תפילין. The source is a ברייתא about מיכל בת כושי wearing תפילין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Women are exempt from a מצות עשה שהזמן גרמא, a positive מצוה tied to specific times. The חכמים allowed מיכל to wear תפילין without objection. The גמרא concludes that they see תפילין as not tied to time at all, so no day is excluded, and that would include שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: מיכל, daughter of שאול המלך, who is called כושי here
The Sages did not protest against her
Going up to ירושלים for the pilgrimage festival
It is evident / this shows that
A positive מצוה not caused or limited by time, which women are obligated in

steps.confusionAlert: Don't read this as a story about women's practice for its own sake. In this סוגיא the story serves only as evidence about the nature of תפילין. If תפילין has no time limits at all, then שבת is also a time for תפילין.
steps.whyThisMatters: The proof rests on a classic link between two topics. A מצוה that applies at all times is one that women are obligated in. A מצוה with excluded times, like שבת, would be time-bound and would exempt women.

phrases.english: Rather, it is this tanna
phrases.notes: Here the גמרא tries a new answer, since the proof from רבי נתן was turned down in Step 15.

phrases.english: as it was taught in a baraita:
Michal, daughter of Kushi
would put on tefillin
and the Sages did not protest against her,
and the wife of Jonah
would go up for the Festival pilgrimage
and the Sages did not protest against her.
From the fact that the Sages did not protest against her
phrases.notes: The proof here comes from מיכל and her תפילין.

phrases.english: it is evident that they hold

phrases.aramaic: מִצְוַת עֲשֵׂה שֶׁלֹּא הַזְּמַן גְּרָמָא הִיא.
phrases.english: that it is a positive מצוה not bound by time.
phrases.notes: If no time is excluded, then שבת is also a time for תפילין

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected רבי נתן answer with a new candidate תנא
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא holds that שבת is a time for תפילין?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The חכמים who did not protest when מיכל wore תפילין, because they hold that תפילין is not bound by time

steps.title: Beginning to push back: perhaps that tanna holds otherwise
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins to reject the proof from מיכל with ״ודילמא סבר לה״. The full rejection continues on the next amud.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a rejection of the proof from מיכל. Only the opening words appear here, and the actual counter-explanation comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ״ודילמא״ ("but perhaps") signals that the proof is not airtight. The גמרא is about to offer a different way to understand the view of these חכמים. Under that reading, it would not follow that שבת is a time for תפילין.

keyTerms.meaning: But perhaps; a standard opening for rejecting a proof
He holds (a certain view)

phrases.english: But perhaps he holds
phrases.notes: The sentence continues on the next amud

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts rejecting the proof brought in Step 16
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The inference from the חכמים not protesting against מיכל
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתא may fit a different view; the details follow on the next amud
